newsitem.title: SPAIN: Cepsa aims to garner North African niche.
newsitem.headline: Cepsa aims to garner North African niche.

text.p: Spanish energy group Cepsa aims to increase its international presence by developing its North African operations, thus obtaining a key position in the area, chairman Carlos Perez de Bricio said on Tuesday.

The Koubha field in Algeria which it plans to operate with Algerian state oil company Sonatrach, is now facing bureaucratic delays, but prospects are good as reserves are bigger than originally thought at roughly 10 times the size of Cepsa's other Algerian field.
"This is the biggest oil field found there in around 20 years," Perez de Bricio told journalists.
Cepsa does not expect to be able to enter the field until the end of 1998, pending local government approval.
It will require a total investment of around $500 million from the groups involved. Cepsa will provide roughly half of that figure over a period of up to about four years.
Reserves cannot be quantified at present, but the field may produce a total 20,000 barrels per day after the year 2000.

Elsewhere in north Africa, the chairman said Cepsa had formed an agreement in Morocco with a local firm to distribute products and hopes to establish a service station network similar to that in Portugal.
Cepsa now has around 100 service stations in Portugal, and has asphalt sales at around 20 percent market share.
Additionally, in January Cepsa bought ELF's 35 service station network in Portugal, aiming for a stronger position in that country.
"We are now frankly well-situated in the Portuguese market," Perez de Bricio said.

Perez de Bricio said the firm also aims to produce petro-chemicals in India which will require an outlay of around 10 billion pesetas. This project is currently being negotiated, and may be announced within a few months.
